newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil posts $26 mln trade gap to May 16.
newsitem.headline: Brazil posts $26 mln trade gap to May 16.

text.p: Brazil posted a $26 million trade deficit up to May 16, with imports of $2.612 billion and exports of $2.586 billion, said a spokeswoman for the Ministry of Industry and Commerce.
The spokeswoman said average daily imports in the first three weeks of the month stood at $237.5 million, and average daily exports at $235.1 million.
Brazil posted a trade surplus of $77 million in the first two weeks of May, with exports of $1.418 billion and imports of $1.341 billion.
April's result was a $951 million trade gap, bringing the deficit for the first four months of the year to just under $4.0 billion, compared with $5.5 billion for the whole of 1996.
Government officials have said they expected a better result in May because of the continuing soybean harvest and measures to stem imports and boost exports.
